name: AgentSpec
description: AgentSpec defines the configurable properties of an agent.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Human-readable description for UI and marketplace display.

fields.name: IconUrl
fields.description:
Icon URL for marketplace and UI display.
 Must be a publicly accessible URL to an image (SVG, PNG, or JPEG).

fields.name: Instructions
fields.description: System prompt defining the agent's behavior and personality.

fields.name: SkillRefs
fields.description: Skill resources providing additional knowledge to the agent.

fields.name: Env
fields.description:
Environment variable declarations for this agent.
 Keys are variable names; values describe their metadata and optionality.
 A secret is found by its name in a vault when a run starts; a plain
 setting may carry its value in the declaration.

fields.name: Tools
fields.description:
Tools this agent may use; empty means every tool it has.

 Entries use Claude Code's names: a built-in such as Read, Grep, Bash,
 Write, Edit, Glob, Agent or WebFetch; mcp__<server> for every tool of one
 MCP server, mcp__<server>__<tool> for one tool, and mcp__* for every MCP
 tool. A plugin's server is named plugin_<plugin>_<server>, as Claude Code
 names it, with every character outside letters, digits, _ and - written
 as _. A specifier in parentheses, as in Bash(git push *), is
 accepted and governs the whole tool. Agent(explore, release-notes)
 also limits which subagents this agent may start; the Cursor engine
 cannot hold its built-in subagents back, so it refuses a turn whose agent
 limits Agent to types. The lists hold on both engines, and under "approve everything"
 too.

 Skill is a name here too, for the agent's skills: a list without Skill
 keeps them, and a list holding only Skill names them, so it does not
 refuse the turn, also under an outer list that omits Skill (a
 plugin subagent's under its turn's, a turn's under the agent's). Denying
 Skill in disallowed_tools removes them, and then a list of Skill alone
 in a narrower layer refuses the turn.

fields.name: DisallowedTools
fields.description:
Tools this agent may never use, in the same names as tools.
 Applied before tools, so a tool named in both is excluded.

 Disallowing Skill hides every skill from this agent: no skill is listed
 or mounted for its turns, and the Read tool refuses reads of skill and
 plugin-tree files. Grep, Glob and a shell the agent is granted are not
 refused, so they can still reach those files.

fields.name: Hooks
fields.description:
Hooks written in this agent itself, run around its tool calls and its
 subagents' calls, after the hooks of the plugins it lists.

 A hook can refuse a call, ask a person first, or let it run
 without the approval it would otherwise need. Both engines run hooks in
 Claude Code's format and in Cursor's. On the Cursor engine, web fetch and
 web search reach no hook, so an agent whose PreToolUse hooks would match
 them runs there without those tools; a PostToolUse hook on them does not
 run there.

fields.name: RunConfig
fields.description:
The author's run defaults: the model, speed tier, thinking and run
 bounds a turn on this agent uses unless the message or the surface it
 came through sets its own (RunConfig has the rule). Versioned with the
 agent, so a conversation pinned to a version keeps that version's
 defaults.

 A choice here (model_name, service_tier, thinking_mode) applies only on
 the engine named in harness; on a conversation running the other engine
 only the bounds apply. A bound here is a cap: a message or a surface can
 lower it, never raise it. A model must be named together with harness,
 and must be one that engine lists; service_tier FAST and thinking_mode
 ENABLED need a model that engine prices or marks capable. Checked when
 the agent is saved.

fields.name: Harness
fields.description:
The engine this agent's run defaults were chosen for, and the engine a
 new conversation on this agent starts on when the person or the surface
 starting it names neither an engine nor a model (a turn that names a
 model but no engine starts on native, the engine its name was checked
 against). Unspecified: the platform's default engine (native).

 Model names belong to an engine (each lists its own), so run_config's
 model, tier and thinking count only on this engine. A conversation keeps
 the engine it started on; a later version naming another engine changes
 only new conversations.

fields.name: Plugins
fields.description:
Plugins this agent uses, each whole: its skills, agents, hooks and MCP
 servers. A server written in the agent itself goes in mcp_servers.

fields.name: Subagents
fields.description:
Saved agents this agent may hand work to, each running its own
 instructions, model, tools, plugins, skills, hooks and values.

 A subagent runs as the conversation's person and on its budget, under
 the conversation's hooks, and cannot hand work on to another agent: an
 agent that lists subagents of its own is refused here. Each reference is
 pinned when this agent is saved: a reference without a version takes the
 listed agent's latest version, and one naming a tag or a version keeps
 that version until a later save sends the list again. At most 20.

fields.name: McpServers
fields.description:
MCP servers written in this agent itself, reached over HTTP, beside the
 servers of the plugins it lists. At most 20.

 Only an organization's admins may add a server or change one's address
 or headers; anyone who may edit the agent may keep or remove them. A
 server's tools are named mcp__<name>__<tool> in tools and
 disallowed_tools. A run logs in with the vault connection saved at the
 server's address, else a vault secret named <NAME>_ACCESS_TOKEN (the
 server's name upper-cased, each other character written as _), which is
 sent to this server, or calls it with no login when there is neither; a
 header that names Authorization itself takes that login from its
 ${NAME} instead, and the run then needs it. Each ${NAME} in a header
 value is filled from the run's values and sent to this server only,
 never to the agent's shell. Header values are stored in the agent, so a
 secret goes in a vault and the header names it.
